briefs.source_chain: AI-financing fears ease (META offering, AVGO funding) + hyperscaler earnings/capex anticipation + CLS beat and an oversold bounce, therefore AI-complex baskets (neocloud/optical/inference-chip/memory/semis) rally sharply, therefore tech leads a broad index rebound (NDX/R2K/SPX up) even as breadth stays weak and momentum recovers off its drawdown, with desk flow skewed better-for-sale from long-onlys against hedge-fund buying.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: AI financing relief + hyperscaler earnings anticipation + CLS beat/oversold bounce, therefore AI baskets outperform, therefore tech-led broad rebound with weak breadth and recovering momentum, with LO supply vs. HF demand flows.

distortions.what: Brief drops the specific $12.2m top-of-book liquidity level, keeping only the +25% vs. 5-day-average figure.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the directional read (liquidity improving) is unchanged; only a supporting absolute figure is dropped.

distortions.what: Brief omits the desk's own activity-level read ('3 out of 10 across the floor').
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is a secondary intensity gauge, not a call or figure status.

distortions.what: Brief compresses the hedge-fund flow detail, dropping which sectors HFs were buying/selling (comms/tech/financials vs. cons disc/macro) and keeping only the 10% better-to-buy headline.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the net HF skew direction (buying) is preserved; only sector granularity is lost.

briefs.source_chain: US tech rebound spreads into Asia but fades as oil rises, therefore the desk stays cautious ahead of central-bank decisions and mega-cap earnings, reading recent bounces as easing selling rather than renewed buying, therefore individual prints (Cadence/Celestica/Orange beat-and-raise; Tieto/Informa guidance cuts) and separate telecom/satellite items (Verizon's own cost-and-timeline defense against SpaceX; the EU's unrelated spectrum-reservation policy against Starlink/Kuiper) round out the day's color as independent items.
briefs.brief_chain: Same macro/earnings chain, but the brief links Verizon's tone-hardening to the EU spectrum decision with 'as,' presenting two independent desk items as cause and effect.

distortions.what: Brief states Verizon's tone hardened 'as the EU moved to reserve satellite spectrum against Starlink and Kuiper,' but the source reports these as two separate, unrelated items: Verizon's tone shift is explained by its own cost/build-time analysis of a competing SpaceX network, while the EU spectrum story is a distinct European policy item with no stated link to Verizon's commentary.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — no trade or stance is built on this link; it is a narrative compression that invents a causal connection between two true, independently-reported facts without changing any desk call.

distortions.what: Brief drops Informa's caveat that shifting events to 2027 does not remove the risk of further US-Iran escalation or prolonged disruption, and the desk's personal 'no rush' framing on buying the dip.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the core call (guidance cut, risk largely anticipated, earnings maintained) is preserved; only a secondary risk caveat is dropped.

distortions.what: Brief drops 'no read in Europe' when reporting Celestica's beat-and-raise as positive for Flex/AVGO/ANET.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the US read-through named in the brief is accurate; omitting the Europe non-read doesn't change any named stock's direction.

distortions.what: Brief omits the UMG private-equity talks and AMAT's stake increase in BESI entirely, though both are named in the source title.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these are separate, self-contained items; their absence doesn't distort any claim the brief does make.

briefs.source_chain: Fed holds as expected but Warsh's dovish, backward-looking communication (missing leading inflation indicators, two dissents for a hike) raises policy-mistake risk, therefore the curve steepens and the dollar weakens, therefore Handelsbanken keeps its December-hike call on a healthy GDP/labor outlook despite Warsh's own admission that conditions aren't tight; separately, the FOMC cuts its meeting count from next autumn.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: hold as expected, two dissents, unexpectedly dovish Warsh resembling the July delivery raises policy-mistake risk, curve steepens/dollar weakens, Handelsbanken keeps the December hike call on GDP/labor strength despite Warsh's 'not tight' admission; separate meeting-count cut.

distortions.what: Brief drops the source's 'rearview mirror' framing — that Warsh ignores leading indicators, growth/inflation drivers, and anchored-but-rising inflation expectations — keeping only the GDP/labor justification for the December call.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the call itself (December hike) and its headline rationale are both preserved; only supporting critique detail is compressed.

briefs.source_chain: SOX's two up days and an Asia rally raise the 'is the worst over' question, therefore Prime data show momentum/leverage positioning has washed out substantially in places, therefore semis fundamentals (rising capex/EPS, cheap valuation) keep improving while investors stay reluctant to re-enter until the market rewards revisions, and the picture isn't fully clean (elevated Nasdaq futures length, weakening CTA trend signals), so: fundamentals improving, positioning messy, machines indifferent.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same bottom line (fundamentals improving, positioning messy, machines don't care).

distortions.what: Brief drops 'dynamic' from Callahan's description of the stretch as 'one of the more dynamic & painful stretches,' rendering it as 'one of the most painful.'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — a single descriptive adjective is dropped from a direct quote; the substance of the quote (fundamentals rising, valuations cheap, reluctance to re-enter) is intact.
